description: Main window capability. http is scoped to the pairing surfaces only (ts.net home serves over Tailscale HTTPS on any port — the pattern must carry `:*`, because URLPattern treats an omitted port as the default port only, so a bare `https://*.ts.net` admitted 443 and refused the 8443/10000 that `tailscale serve` also hands out, GDK-1048) — the packaged app talks to nothing else. Loopback is NOT here: the shipped phone has nothing on its own 127.0.0.1, and the capability file is the one place the App Store binary's ACL is decided — loopback rides dev-loopback.json instead, pinned to non-iOS targets (GDK-1581; Tauri v2 has no dev/release capability split, so target platform is the only lever that keeps it out of the .ipa while the test corpus below still unions to the TS predicate's scope). There is no websocket permission anymore (GDK-897): the PTY socket is dialled by the shell_ws_* commands in src-tauri/src/shell.rs, which build the URL from the stored pairing (shell_pair_set), validate it against this same list (endpoint_in_scope mirrors src/lib/dial-scope.ts verdict for verdict, loopback gated to non-iOS exactly like dev-loopback.json), and read the Bearer from secure storage themselves — the JS side supplies a session id and nothing else, where the plugin's websocket:default grant had no URL allowlist at all and let anything in this webview dial any host on the internet. src/lib/dial-scope.ts still restates this http list as one predicate for the fetch path (asserted before each dial in lib/api.ts and as a pre-flight in lib/terminal/transport.ts). barcode-scanner:default backs the QR pairing scan (src/screens/PairGate.svelte, src/screens/PairingTab.svelte). secure-storage plugin commands are deliberately NOT granted to JS: the token_get/token_set/token_del commands in lib.rs are the only door to the token. deep-link:default (GDK-873) only lets JS subscribe to URLs the OS already routed to this app — the scheme is declared in Info.ios.plist, this permission does not widen what may be dialed, and the gadak:// grammar carries no verb, so the worst a hostile link achieves is that the user looks at the wrong issue.
